s: rich, containing a lot of fat
In diesem Satz ist nur das Wort „fett“ fett geschrieben.

Sie hat 'nen fetten Vertrag an Land gezogen.

fett.et: From Middle Low German vet, from Old Saxon *fētid, from Proto-West Germanic *faitid. Doublet of feist. In the colloquial sense perhaps a calque of English phat via hip-hop culture.

From Middle High German vetze (“rag, tatters”), ultimately from the root of fassen (“to grasp”).
Cognate with Proto-Germanic *fatą (“vat, item of clothing”), Old Norse fǫt (“clothes”), Portuguese fato (“clothing”), Spanish hato.
